title: How we're balancing player agency and continuity in an AI story game
author: Anime-Tales
selftext:
I'm a dev of Anime-Tales, a playable AI interactive story game. Players create a character, build or choose a world, and play solo or with friends. I wanted to share one of the design problems we're working through rather than just drop a trailer.



A custom world can have a world bible, cast details, rules, places, and lore entries. The story uses those details to keep the setting and characters coherent across turns. At the same time, sandbox mode is meant to let a player declare surprising new facts and take the story somewhere we did not script. Too much rigidity makes that feel fake; too little continuity makes choices feel disposable.



I'm curious how other AI game developers handle this. When a player contradicts a world rule or a character's established history, should the game accept it, ask for clarification, or turn the contradiction into a story event? If you've run into a concrete failure mode, I'd love to hear it.



For context, the playable game is at https://anime-tales.com/.
